lawyer:
Shahidul Alam Chowdhury, Advocate, instructed by Md. Aftab Hossain, Advocate-on-Record — For the Petitioner. 
Abdur Rab, Advocate-on-Record — For the Respondents.
parties:
Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka ------ Plaintiff-Appellant
Vs.
Abdur Rab, constituted Attorney of Zamila Khatun and ors Defendant ------ Respondents
full_judgment: Late Al-haj Duliluddin Ahmed (died on 6-2-82), the predecessor-in-interest of the defendant-respondents of both the appeals instituted on 8-9-78 Title Suit No. 243 of 1978 in the court of then Munsif, 6th Court, now Assistant Judge, Dhaka for khas possession of the suit premises, against the custodian of vested property as defendant No. 1 and the present plaintiff-appellant, the Additional Deputy Commissioner (Revenue) Dhaka, as defendant No. 2 alleging, inter alia, that on 26-12-61 he has auction purchased, in a certificate case under the Public Demands Recovery Act, the suit properties comprising of Municipal Holding Nos. 26 and 26/1, Kali Charan Shaha Road, within Sutrapur police station, District Dhaka. The auction sale was confirmed on 9-9-66 and formal symbolical possession was given to him on 22-7-71. But the defendants illegally kept the suit property under their possession. The suit was decreed ex parte on 3-6-80. The decree-holder then filed Title Execution Case No. 14 of 1981. The present appellant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 47 of 1981, under Order 9 rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the said ex-parte decree, which, however, was dismissed for default on 15-6-81 and then his application under section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the said Miscellaneous case was also rejected on 27-2- 82. One MA Khaleque, who claimed himself as a monthly tenant in respect of the suit premises under the present appellant, on 11-5-81 instituted Title Suit No. 509 of 1981 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for declaration that the aforesaid ex-parte decree was illegal, void, etc. making the present appellant as well as the Government of Bangladesh as defendant No. 5 and 3 respectively and on 13-7-81 got an order of temporary injunction restraining the decree-holder-respondent from proceeding with the said title execution case pending disposal of the suit. The suit was dismissed and the same was maintained by the High Court Division by its judgment and order dated 10-3-83 passed in Civil Revision No. 116 of 1982. On 26-6-82 the present appellant filed Title Suit No. 294 of 1982, subsequently renumbered as Title Suit No. 210 of 1991, for setting aside the aforesaid ex parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 243 of 1987 and the same was dismissed for default on 4-6-94. Against which the appellant filed Miscellaneous Case No. 33 of 1994, renumbered as Miscellaneous Case No.17 of 1995, under Order 9 rule 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit alleging, inter that on 4-6-94 the learned Advocate had been engaged in another court and accordingly, he filed an application for adjournment but the court dismissed the suit before noon without considering the prayer for adjournment.
